| `test "n", {target: f, satisfies: %i[nist_cm_7 nist_ac_6]}` | `test "n", {satisfies: %i[nist_ac_6 nist_cm_7], target: f}` | one tree: a declaration is a set of controls and one target, so the parser builds one order, and the test's `def_hash` and `blue query` see one shape. The map is the options' own literal (a call takes no bare entries without `**`, spec row `maps.spread.call.entries_need_a_spread`), as `virtualize(cap, {using: …})` takes settings. Corpus: 0 (new, 2026-10-30) | parser (builds the order) | B0068 | autofix |
| `if c … else nil end`, an empty `else` | `if c … end` | an `if` that fails is already nil. Corpus: 85 | parser (drops the branch) | B0035 | autofix (kept when the `else` holds a comment) |
| `car`, `cdr`, `next`, `modulo`, `rem`, `bool?`, `comp`, `foldl`, `some?(x)`, `error_kind(e)`, `error_message(e)` | `first`, `rest`, `rest`, `a % b`, `a % b`, `boolean?`, `compose`, `reduce`, `x != nil`, `e.kind`, `e.message` | readability: the name a reader without Lisp knows; `some?` reads as "some element". Each pair measured equal on every input class (`blue eval`, 2026-10-19). Corpus: 2 `car`, 12 `cdr`, 34 `modulo`, 13 `foldl`, 2 `bool?`, 7 `nil?` | resolution | B0036 | autofix; writes `blue::first` where a listed import shadows the bare name |
| `throw(error(k, m))`, `throw(x)`, `try(x, catch(e(), h))`, `begin … end` as a whole `def` body | `raise(k, m)`, `raise(x)`, `x rescue h` or `begin … rescue e … end`, the clauses on the `def` | readability: one step to raise, a block that reads like Ruby's, the error a readable record. Corpus: 92 `throw(error(`, 178 `throw(`, 212 `try(` | resolution (`throw`), parser (`try`, `begin`) | B0037 | autofix |
| `apply(f, a, xs)` with `f` a name | `f(a, *xs)` | one tree; the call keeps its shape. Corpus: 41 | parser, formatter | B0042 | autofix |
| `(x) -> f(x)` with `f` a `def` of the file taking exactly those parameters | `f` | one function, the shorter name; `fn … end` on one line is B0024 | check stage | B0044 | autofix |
| `to_s(to_s(x))`, `string(trim(x))`, `to_int(to_int!(x))`, `to_float(sqrt(x))`, `trim(trim(x))`, `to_s("a")`: a conversion whose argument is a builtin call that already returns the kind it leaves alone, or a literal of that kind | the argument itself | the chain does nothing; one table, `blue_lang_check::chains::RULES`, read by the check stage, the formatter and the evaluator, each row carrying an okite law (D0013). `to_int(to_int(x))`, `to_float(to_float(x))` and `upcase(downcase(x))` stay: they change values. A local or definition named like the builtin is never rewritten | check stage, evaluator | B0045 | autofix |
| `if getenv("X_MAIN", "") == "1" … f … end` | `def main()`, called by `blue run` | one entry-point convention; no environment variable. Corpus: 8 | check stage | B0041 | autofix where the guard calls one zero-parameter function used nowhere else; refused otherwise |
| `ro_resolve_argv`, `ro_patch_argv`, `ro_main` in a program | `resolve_argv`, `patch_argv`, `main` | the file is the namespace; a prefix repeats it. Corpus: the nix programs and the `gen/` generators | check stage | B0043 | autofix where no stripped name is already used in the file or reserved; refused otherwise (a bidama's prefix is B0013/B0014) |
| `rescue e` with an empty or `nil` handler | `rescue _` and `nil`, or `x rescue nil` | silence must be visible | check stage | B0038 | refused |
| two tests with one name | distinct names | a failure must say which test | check stage | B0039 | refused |
| `retryCount` | `retry_count` | readability: one case for names. Corpus: 1 | check stage | B0040 | refused (a name is its callers' too) |
| whitespace, indentation, width 80, blank lines, redundant parentheses, a call whose one argument is a literal broken over lines | `blue fmt`'s layout | one layout; a short call stays on its line | formatter | B0024 | autofix |
| `name()` for a zero-parameter function | `name` | (shipped in v0.0.74) | resolution | B0023 | autofix |
| a `use` out of order, twice, or unread | sorted, once, read | (shipped) | check stage | B0015, B0016 | list sort and `use` form order: autofix; unused: refused |
| a bare name reached only through a bidama another `use` loaded; `retsu::first` with no `use("retsu")` | `use("retsu", [:first, :last])` added in package order; `use("retsu")` added | the file says what it reads | check stage | B0012, B0010 | autofix in a script (a bidama's Bluefile `needs` is the author's) |
| `blue::name` where the bare name is the builtin | `name` | (shipped) | resolution | B0018 | autofix |
| a `#` comment block documenting a `def`; a heredoc indented, with trailing spaces or edge blank lines; a blank line between `@doc` and its `def` | `@doc """` … `"""` at column 0 directly above the `def`; `@moduledoc` as the file's first form | documentation is a typed child of the definition, not a comment: it is in the tree, in `def_hash`, and its `expr #=> value` lines run as tests. The text is data (no escapes, no interpolation); its indentation is presentation, stripped at lex time. Corpus: 0 `@doc` before 2026-10-24 | parser (lexes the heredoc, builds `blue-doc`), formatter | B0024; B0056 lifts the `#` line | autofix |

## New forms these rules write

- **Logic words**: `and`, `or`, `not` are reserved. `not` binds as `!` did
  (tightly), and a negation that is an operand of a comparison or arithmetic is
  written `(not a) == b`.
- **Errors**: `raise(:kind, "message")`, `raise(:kind, "message", {data: d, cause: e})`,
  `raise(e)`. `x rescue fallback` binds loosest of all, below `|>`. A block:
  `begin … rescue :a, :b as e … rescue e … ensure … end`; a `def` takes the same
  clauses directly. An uncaught error prints `kind: message`, every cause, and
  the stack, and exits 1. The error value's fields: `e.kind`, `e.message`,
  `e.data`, `e.cause`, `e.trace` (the raise site, `file:line`); `"#{e}"` is
  `kind: message (at file:line)`.
- **Declared records**: `record point(x, y: Int)` at a file's top level is the
  one spelling of a named structure; `struct` and `class` before a name are parse
  errors naming it. By name is the map a call already takes, `point({x: 1, y: 2})`,
  and an update is the spread a call already takes, `point(**p, x: 3)`, so the
  form adds no second call spelling (okite D0017, B0079).
- **Records**: `x.name` without parentheses reads a field: a map's keyword or
  string key, a keyed list (`exec_capture`'s `[[:status, n], …]`, a parsed JSON
  object), or an error's field. A missing field raises naming the fields there
  are; `get(m, :k)` reads a field that may be absent.
- **Splat**: `f(a, *xs)`, the list last.
- **Entry point**: `def main()`, called by `blue run` and by nothing else.
- **Test declarations**: `test "n", {satisfies: [:nist_ac_6], target: parse_token}`
  lowers to `(deftest "n" (blue-test-meta (hash-map :satisfies (list
  :nist_ac_6) :target parse_token)) body)`: the map literal's own tree under
  a head only the harness binds, so the declaration is data the harness, the
  check stage and `blue query` read, and the target is a reference the
  resolver names (`%root/parse_token`) and never calls. A control is a
  catalog keyword (`blue_lang_check::controls::oscal_id`, B0069).
- **Breach assertions**: `assert_panics expr` lowers to `(blue-assert-panics
  'expr (lambda () expr))`, `assert`'s shape plus the function the harness
  moves into a child held to a pure frame. One spelling: `assert_panics(expr)`
  is the same tree, its parentheses only grouping (B0024).
- **Libraries**: `deeta::json_at(doc, "spec.items.0.name")`, nil when any step
  is absent; `saishikou::retrying({times: 3, wait_ms: 500, on: [:timeout]}, fn() … end)`.

## Considered and not made rules

| forms | decision | why |
|---|---|---|
| `"a" + x` vs interpolation | no second form | `+` is numbers only; `"a#{x}"` is the one spelling |
| `concat(a, b)` vs `"#{a}#{b}"` | both stay | different trees, and `concat` is how a literal `#{` is built (222 calls) |
| `:sym` vs `"sym"` | both stay | different values |
| `x == true` vs `x` | both stay | different meanings under truthiness (2,479 in tests) |
| `eq?` vs `==`, `null?` vs `empty?`, `length` vs `count`, `some` vs `any?` | both stay | different answers on some input (`eq?` is identity; `null?("")`; `length(nil)` raises; `some` answers nil) |
| `count(x) == 0` vs `empty?(x)` | both stay | `count` raises where `empty?` answers; a rewrite would change a failure into a value |
| `if not c a else b end` vs `if c b else a end` | both stay | branch order is the author's emphasis, and swapping it moves comments |
| pipelines | call form | the tree does not remember the spelling; a pipeline rendering for long data-first chains needs a shape detector and is a formatter version bump (§V.13) |
| `def f()` vs `def f` | `def f()` | the definition says it takes nothing; only the call is bare |
| unused locals and parameters | B0002 stays a warning | renaming in flight would rename a parameter the author is about to use |
| `return`, `do`/braces blocks, `;`, `xs[i]` | one form already | refused by the parser with the canonical spelling named |
| a typed `raise :kind, "m"` keyword form | `raise(…)` call | blue has no paren-less calls; one call grammar |
| Result values and a `?` operator | not added | exceptions stay the one error model; `kyohi` holds refusals as data where a caller branches on them |
| retry as syntax (`retry`) | a bidama, `saishikou` | a bounded helper says its bound; a keyword hides a loop |
| a warning for rescuing a kind nothing raises | not built | no analysis can know which kinds a call raises |
| `test "n" satisfies: …` without braces, or `@satisfies` above a test | the map after a comma | a call takes no bare entries without `**`, and an attribute is a second form to read for one test; the map is the literal the house already passes settings in |
| a block `assert_panics … end` | `assert_panics expr` | `assert`'s shape; several statements are a function, called |

---

Source: `docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md`

# Diagnostics

What blue's check stage reports, and the machine-readable shape of it.

Every rule lives in one registry, `blue_lang_check::RULES`
(`crates/blue-lang-check/src/rules.rs`). The check stage runs on every door —
`blue run`, `blue test`, `blue check`, the language server and every bidama
build — so an error-severity rule is a program that does not run or build.
`blue explain CODE` prints a rule's explanation and an example that violates
it; `blue explain --list` lists them.

## Codes

| code | slug | severity | law |
|---|---|---|---|
| B0001 | unbound-name | error | every name a program uses is bound |
| B0002 | unused-binding | warning | a local binding is read at least once, or its name starts with `_` |
| B0003 | return-type-mismatch | error | a typed definition's body produces its declared type |
| B0004 | operand-type-mismatch | error | an operator in a typed definition gets operands of its type |
| B0005 | argument-type-mismatch | error | a call to a typed definition passes the declared types |
| B0006 | syntax-error | error | a file parses |
| B0007 | malformed-waiver | error | a waiver names a known, waivable code and gives a reason |
| B0008 | unused-waiver | error | a waiver suppresses at least one diagnostic |
| B0009 | ambiguous-name | error | no two namespaces in one resolution tier define a name |
| B0010 | qualifier-not-imported | error | a qualified name's level is one the file `use`s or one below it |
| B0011 | no-such-definition | error | a qualified name, or a name a `use` lists, is a definition of that level |
| B0012 | implicit-reference | error | a bare name that is another bidama's definition is one the file lists, or is written qualified |
| B0013 | prefixed-definition | error | a bidama's definition does not spell its bidama |
| B0014 | mangled-namespace | error | a bidama does not prefix nine in ten of its definitions with one short `x_` |
| B0015 | non-canonical-import | error | a file's `use` forms come first, one per package, sorted, each list sorted |
| B0016 | unused-import | error | every `use` is reached, and every name it lists is read |
| B0017 | duplicate-definition | error | a namespace defines a function or macro once |
| B0018 | redundant-qualifier | error | a qualifier changes what its name means |
| B0019 | needs-mismatch | error | the bidamas a bidama `use`s are exactly the `needs` its Bluefile.lock records (`blue lock` derives them from the `use`s; a Bluefile `needs` row only narrows a range) |
| B0020 | package-as-value | error | a bidama's name is written as a qualifier, never as a value |
| B0021 | legacy-name | error | a renamed or moved definition is called by its new name; the old one is a bridge that closes at the next minor version |
| B0022 | legacy-misuse | error | a `legacy_names` declaration is one of each form per bidama, dated from a version it has reached, names no name twice, and moves a name only to a definition a loaded bidama holds |
| B0023 | bare-nullary-call | error | a call to a function that takes no parameters is written bare: `now_ms`, never `now_ms()` |
| B0024 | layout | error | a file is laid out as `blue fmt` writes it: indentation, line breaks at 80 columns, blank lines and parentheses |
| B0025 | logical-words | error | logic is written in words: `a and b`, `a or b`, `not x`, never `&&`, `\|\|`, `!` |
| B0026 | unless | error | a negated condition is written `if not c`, never `unless c` |
| B0027 | elsif | error | an `else` whose whole body is an `if` is written `elsif` |
| B0028 | call-form | error | a call is written `f(x, y)`: never `x.f(y)` or `x \|> f(y)` |
| B0029 | keyword-key | error | a map key that is a keyword is written `name: value`, never `:name => value` |
| B0030 | parameter-list | error | a definition and a lambda write their parameter list, even an empty one: `def f()`, `fn() … end` |
| B0031 | operator-spelling | error | an operator or literal is written as itself, never as the call it lowers to or a typographic alias |
| B0032 | trailing-comma | error | no comma before a closing bracket |
| B0033 | literal-spelling | error | a literal is written as `blue fmt` writes its value: digits of six or more grouped `1_000_000`, an invisible character escaped `\u{1b}` |
| B0034 | negated-comparison | error | a negated equality is written with the other operator: `a != b`, never `not (a == b)` |
| B0035 | else-nil | error | an `if` has no `else` whose body is empty or `nil` |
| B0036 | builtin-synonym | error | a builtin with two names is called by its readable one: `first` not `car`, `rest` not `cdr` or `next`, `a % b` not `modulo`/`rem`, `boolean?` not `bool?`, `compose` not `comp`, `reduce` not `foldl`, `x != nil` not `some?(x)`, `e.kind`/`e.message` not `error_kind`/`error_message` |
| B0037 | error-spelling | error | an error is raised with `raise` and caught with `rescue`: never `throw(error(…))` or `try(…, catch(…))` |
| B0038 | swallowed-error | error | a `rescue` that catches every error and does nothing names the error `_` |
| B0039 | duplicate-test-name | error | the tests of a file have distinct names |
| B0040 | identifier-case | error | a function, parameter or local is named in lower snake_case (`retry_count`, never `retryCount`); a top-level constant may be UPPER_SNAKE |
| B0041 | main-guard | error | a program's entry point is `def main()`, which `blue run` calls; never a top-level `if getenv("X_MAIN", "") == "1"` guard |
| B0042 | splat | error | a list passed as a call's last arguments is written `f(a, *xs)`, never `apply(f, a, xs)` with `f` a name |
| B0043 | prefixed-program | error | a program does not prefix every definition with one short `x_`: the file is the namespace |
| B0044 | eta-reduction | error | a function that only forwards its parameters to a named function is that name: `map(describe, vs)`, never `map((v) -> describe(v), vs)` |
| B0046 | map-pun | error | a map entry whose value is the variable of the same name is written `{name:}`, never `{name: name}` |
| B0047 | nil-test | error | a nil test is written `x.nil?`, never `nil?(x)`, `x == nil` or `nil == x` |
| B0045 | redundant-conversion | warning | a conversion is not applied to a value it leaves alone: `to_s(to_s(x))` is `to_s(x)`, never the longer chain |
| B0048 | undeclared-field-read | error | a fragment ref is read only for the fields its fragment declares; a parent never reads a child's field |
| B0049 | fragment-not-composed | error | a view's operation is the union of the fragments of the components it renders: a ref passed to a component comes from a selection that spreads its fragment, and every spread names a declared fragment |
| B0050 | field-not-in-schema | error | every fragment's type and field, and every `labels` enum and key, is in the frontend's schema |
| B0051 | enum-mirror | error | a literal list never mirrors an enum of the schema; display text is keyed by the enum with `labels` |
| B0052 | query-text | error | a view holds no GraphQL operation text; its operation is composed from fragments and sent by hash |
| B0053 | discarded-value | error | the value of a word that only returns a value is read: `assoc`, `append`, `to_s` and their kin are never a statement |
| B0056 | undocumented-definition | error | a bidama's public definition has a `@doc` whose first sentence starts with its name |
| B0057 | doc-without-example | error | a `@doc` holds at least one example, an indented `expr #=> value` line |
| B0058 | undocumented-bidama | error | a bidama's file opens with a `@moduledoc` holding its purpose and one whole example |
| B0059 | placeholder-doc | error | a `@doc` or `@moduledoc` says something: no empty text and no placeholder (`TODO`, `TBD`, `...`) |
| B0060 | restated-doc | error | a `@doc` never restates a type, a signature or a contract field: blue derives them |
| B0061 | undeclared-option | error | a function's option keys are a closed set: a call passes only keys the function reads, and a `checked(opts, [...])` list declares every key the function reads |
| B0062 | argument-kind | error | a value whose kind is known is never passed where a builtin, or the parameter it flows to, takes another kind |
| B0063 | nullary-as-function | error | a zero-argument definition passed where a function is taken is written `() -> name`; a bare zero-argument name is a call |
| B0064 | unformatted-producer | error | a program that writes a `.b` file writes it with `write_program`, which formats it; a producer owns the form of what it emits |
| B0065 | newline-escape | error | text of several lines is written as its lines: `join_lines([a, b])`, `unlines([a, b])` when it ends in a newline, `line_break` alone; never a `\n` escape in a string |
| B0066 | index | error | a key or position is read with brackets: `m[:k]` for `get(m, :k)`, `xs[i]` for `nth(i, xs)` |
| B0067 | name-as-string | error | a name a builtin reads as text is a keyword, not a string: `error(:kind, m)`, `json_get(doc, :field)`, `json_get_or(doc, :field, d)` |
| B0068 | test-declaration-order | error | a test's declaration is written `satisfies` then `target`, its controls sorted: `{satisfies: %i[nist_ac_6 nist_cm_7], target: f}` |
| B0069 | test-declaration | error | a test satisfies controls the catalog table names (`:nist_ac_6` is NIST_SP_800_53R5_AC_6) and targets a definition of the program |
| B0070 | reimplemented-word | warning | a definition of 12 or more nodes is not a catalogue word's shape: it uses the word, or waives this rule with its reason |
| B0071 | evaluator-name | error | a definition is not named for a word the evaluator answers first: a word syntax lowers to (`list`, `concat`, `apply`, `equal?`, `mod`, `join_lines`, `unlines`, `line_break`) or a special form |
| B0072 | call-arity | error | a call to a definition passes a number of arguments that definition takes |
| B0073 | computed-use | error | a `use` names its path as a literal, so the loader and the check stage read it before the program runs |
| B0074 | moved-package | error | a bidama that moved into another bidama's tree is used by its new path; the old name is a bridge that closes at the root's next minor version |
| B0076 | non-canonical-reference | error | a qualified name is written by the full path of the level that defines it, so one definition has one spelling and `rg` finds every caller |
| B0077 | non-canonical-use | error | an import is written `use("a/b")` or `use("a/b", [:x])`: one level, its path as a slash string |
| B0078 | redundant-use | error | a file imports a tree once: a `use` that lists nothing, of a level below another `use` of the file, adds nothing |
| B0079 | record-fields | error | a call of a record's constructor gives every field and no other, and a literal in a typed field has that type |

The registry is the source of truth; a test fails if a code is missing here.

## Ratchets: how a rule becomes an error

A rule the corpus does not yet satisfy is registered with `ratchet: Some(n)`:
it is computed on every program and its findings are counted, not enforced.
`blue census [ROOT]` counts them over every `.b` file under ROOT, and
`checks.namespace-census` fails unless each count equals its row's ratchet
exactly, so every change to a count is a reviewed edit of the number. The
commit that brings a count to zero sets the row to `Some(0)`, and from then
on the rule is an error on every door. `blue census --findings` lists each
finding.

## The reuse ratchet

`blue census --reuse [ROOT]` counts copies per package, against the hadome
baseline `ROOT/reuse.baseline` (`--baseline FILE` to name another). The tool
is `crates/blue-lang-cli/blue/reuse.b`, compiled into the binary.

A copy is a definition of 12 or more nodes (`Near::DEFAULT.min_size`) whose
`shape_hash` is another package's or file's. A row is `reuse-copy: SCOPE N`:
SCOPE is the package, or `%root:FILE` for a script.

| state | exit | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| no baseline | 0 | enforces nothing; prints the measure and the command that adopts it |
| a row held | 0 | |
| a row shrank | 0 | reported; `--record` banks it |
| a row is gone | 0 | advisory; `--record` drops it |
| a row grew, or a scope has no row | 1 | names the row and the copies inside it; every other row, and `run`, `test` and every build, go on |
| a file does not load | 0 | `blind: FILE: why`; counted as blind, never as zero |

`--record` writes the measured rows. It banks a fall with no argument; a raised
or new row is refused without `--receipt "<why>"`, which stays beside the rows
as a `# receipt:` line a reviewer reads. `--json` prints one document with the
rows that broke and each copy's home. `--facts` prints each measured definition
and exits 0. `checks.reuse-ratchet` (`lib.project`) runs the check on every
project, and `pleme-io/actions/blue-reuse` runs it in CI. A project adopts it
with one command, and the file it writes is the only thing that turns it on:

    blue census --reuse . --record --receipt "first measure"

`blue check --reuse FILE` prints each B0070 in one file, with the word to use
and its import line, and always exits 0. `blue check --reuse --hook` reads Claude
Code's PostToolUse JSON from stdin, takes `tool_input.file_path`, stays silent
unless it ends in `.b` and exists, and exits 0 on every failure of its own.

## The data laws (B0048–B0052)

The frontend's data laws (`theory/BLUE-FRONTEND.md` §2) are rows like every
other. A fragment declared with `danpen::fragment(:user_card, {on: "User",
fields: […]})` is the type `UserCard`; a parameter annotated with it holds a
fragment ref, and the typing ladder checks every read of it (B0048) and every
ref passed on to a component (B0049, whose fix adds the spread). The schema
enters through the project's Bluefile: `frontend(name, {views:, schema:})`
names the SDL, and the `generate(...)` whose inputs hold that SDL writes the
table the check reads (`danpen::render(sdl, :table)`), so
`checks.generated-<name>-fresh` keeps it current. A file under a frontend's
`views` is a view (B0052 applies); any other file of the project is checked
against the same table (B0050, B0051). A file with no frontend around it has
no table, and B0050–B0052 do not run for it. In nix a check program runs
alone in the store, so only `blue check`, the language server, `blue census`
and the corpus test read the table there.

`blue_lang_check::data_laws::Fragments` is the fragment and composition table
as data (each fragment's type, fields and spreads), for checks that build on
it.

## Name resolution order

A bare name resolves by tier, first match wins, deterministically
(`blue_lang_check::names::RESOLUTION_ORDER`): locals innermost first, then
the referencing file's own bidama (or, for a script, the file), then the
names the file lists in its `use` forms (`use("retsu", [:first])`), then
builtins (harness names, special forms, macros, values). A `use("x")` with no
list makes `x::name` reachable and no bare name; a bidama the file does not
`use` is not visible. Two namespaces in the tier that holds the name is B0009
(two lists naming it). A qualified name — `retsu::first`, or `blue::first`
for the builtin — bypasses the tiers and is exact.

The words the parser lowers its own syntax to (`blue_lang_syntax::LOWERED_HEADS`:
`list` for `[…]`, `concat` for interpolation, `not`, `and`, `or`, `mod`,
`equal?`, `not=`, `apply`) skip the own and listed tiers: a bare one is always
the builtin, so a bidama may define `list` and its literals still build lists.
Its own definition is reached qualified (`gitto::list`), and `B0018` does not
call that qualifier redundant. `get` is not among them: field access lowers to
`blue-field`, so a bidama may define `get` and use `x.name` freely.

The runtime evaluates the tree resolution produced: every definition keyed
`pkg/name` (`%root/name` for a script), every reference to it as that key, a
builtin bare. So the runtime binds exactly what the check resolved.

## Overrides, and `blue explain-name`

When a bare name is bound in one tier while a lower tier also holds it — a
bidama's own `count` over the builtin, a listed `first` over the builtin — the
higher tier wins; that is the order, not an error, since each tier is
something the author wrote. `blue check --format json` records each one in
the entry file as a line after the diagnostics:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `override` |
| `name` | the name as written |
| location fields | where the reference is |
| `tier` | the tier that won: `own` or `imported` |
| `namespace` | the winning namespace: a bidama's name, or `this file` |
| `shadowed` | each lower-tier candidate, as `{tier, namespace}` |

`blue explain-name NAME FILE:LINE` prints the whole path for one name at one
place: each tier, what it holds, and which wins.

## Waivers

The one escape hatch is a comment directly above a top-level definition:

```
# waive B0002: the callback shape is fixed
def on_event(event, ctx)
  event
end
```

It suppresses that code inside that definition and nowhere else. There is no
file-wide or global waiver. A waived diagnostic is still reported: `blue check`
counts it, and `--format json` lists it with its `waiver` set.

## `blue check --format json`

JSON Lines on stdout: one object per diagnostic per line, reported ones first,
then waived ones. The exit status is 1 when any error-severity diagnostic is
reported. The field names below are stable; `crates/blue-lang-cli/tests/check_json.rs`
pins the exact output and fails if a field here is undocumented.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | the rule, `B0001` |
| `slug` | string | the rule's kebab-case name, `unbound-name` |
| `severity` | string | `error` or `warning` |
| `message` | string | what is wrong, one line |
| `file` | string or null | the file the primary span is in (an imported bidama's own path when the fault is there) |
| `line`, `column` | number or null | start, 1-based; columns count characters, not bytes |
| `end_line`, `end_column` | number or null | end (exclusive), same units |
| `byte_start`, `byte_end` | number or null | the half-open byte range in `file` |
| `help` | string or null | one line on what to do |
| `related` | array | other places: each has the location fields above and a `message` |
| `fixes` | array | suggested repairs, best first |
| `waiver` | object or null | set when a waiver suppressed this diagnostic: `reason`, and the waiver's `line` |

Each entry of `fixes`:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `message` | what the fix does, `replace with \`length\` (builtin)` |
| `applicability` | `machine-applicable` (preserves meaning; `--fix` applies it) or `maybe-incorrect` (a guess; never applied automatically) |
| `edits` | byte-range replacements applied together: the location fields, `original` (what the range must still contain, or the edit is refused) and `replacement` |

A location is `null` throughout when it cannot be placed honestly (for
example, a span that is not a range in the named file).

## `blue run --format json`

A runtime error as one JSON object on stdout, the same error `blue run` prints
as text: `stage` (`eval`), `severity`, `message` (names as the author writes
them), `file`, `line`, `column` (each `null` when it cannot be justified), and
`stack`, the blue call stack innermost first, each frame `function`, `file`,
`line`, `column`, or `builtin: true` for a builtin the runtime defines in
tatara-lisp. The last frame is `<top level>` when the whole stack was
recorded; `stack_depth` counts every frame unwound, recorded or not (a trace
keeps 256). Any other stage's error is `stage` (`parse`, `check`, `import`)
and `message`. `crates/blue-lang-cli/tests/observe.rs` pins the shape.

## `blue check --fix`

Applies every machine-applicable fix whose edits land in the named file and
still match their `original`, skips overlapping ones, then re-formats and
re-checks the file and reports what remains. Suggestions marked
`maybe-incorrect` are never applied.

`blue check --fix --only CODE FILE` (repeatable) applies only those codes'
fixes, to the file as written: no re-format, no project-rule fix, no Bluefile
edit. A project pinned to an older blue takes one rule's fix from a newer blue
this way, then formats with its own (`blue fmt --write`).

## Project rules

A project adds its own check rules, written in blue, by naming them in its
Bluefile:

```
rule("R0001", "rules/conventions.b", "nil_predicate")
rule("R0002", "rules/conventions.b", "loud_call", "warning")
```

`rule(code, file, def[, severity])` names a definition in a blue file (relative
to the Bluefile). `blue check FILE` gathers the rules of every Bluefile in
FILE's directory and its ancestors, up to the directory holding `.git`, and
calls each one on every top-level form of FILE, beside the registry. A code
declared by two Bluefiles is refused.

**Codes.** A project code is one to four capital letters, never `B` alone,
then four digits (`R0001`, `KZ0003`). `B` + four digits is blue's registry, so
the two never meet. Severity is `error` (the default) or `warning`.

**The ABI.** The definition takes one argument, a top-level form as data (the
tree the parser wrote, as a macro sees its arguments: symbols, lists, `quote`
as `(quote x)`), and returns a list of findings. A finding is a map:

| key | | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `at` | required | the path to the node, one child index per level; `[]` is the form itself |
| `message` | required | a string |
| `help` | optional | a string |
| `fix` | optional | a tree that replaces the node at `at`, usually built with `quote … unquote(x) … end` |

```
def nil_predicate(form)
  hits = filter(fn(p) call?(last(p), "nil?", 1) end, nodes(form, []))
  map(
    fn(p)
      arg = nth(1, last(p))
      {at: first(p), message: "write `x.nil?`", fix: quote
        unquote(arg).nil?
      end}
    end,
    hits
  )
end
```

The code and severity are the Bluefile row's. A path, not a byte offset: the
rule sees only data, and `blue check` resolves the path against the form it
gave the rule, so the rule needs no access to the source (and can later run as
a wasm module, `theory/BLUE-EXECUTION.md` §I.2). A fix is rendered by the
formatter and proved before `--fix` will apply it: the edited file is parsed
and must hold exactly the rule's tree at that path (the rendering is retried in
parentheses when an operator binds differently in place); otherwise it is
offered as `maybe-incorrect`.

**The frame.** A rule program, imported bidamas included, may name every
builtin except the host effects (process, filesystem, environment, clock,
network), printing, and `eval`, `require` and `provide`. A rule that names one
is refused before it runs. Each call runs under a step budget
(`blue_lang_runtime::project_rules::RULE_STEPS`).

**Failures.** A rule that does not load, reaches outside its frame, raises,
runs past its budget, or returns anything but a list of findings is reported
once, as an error under its code with the slug `rule-failure`, and is not run
on the file's remaining forms. The other rules still report.

**Waivers** use the one grammar: `# waive R0001: reason` above the definition.
The check stage that `blue run`, `blue test` and every build run does not run
project rules, so it leaves a project-code waiver alone; `blue check` reports
one that names no declared rule (B0007) or suppresses nothing (B0008).

**Output.** Findings are diagnostics in every format above: `file:line:col:
error[R0001]: message`, the same JSON object (the slug is the definition's
name, kebab-cased), the same `fixes`. `blue check` prints `project rules: N`
when any apply.

**In nix**, a project whose Bluefile declares rules gets
`checks.project-rules-hold`: `blue check` on every `.b` file of its packages and
every run, check and app program.

## `blue ast --resolved --json`

How every name in a file resolves, under both rules: today's **flat** rule
(one global environment; the definition evaluated last wins, a builtin only
when no program form defines the name) and **per-bidama namespaces** (locals,
then the file's own package, then its explicit imports, then builtins; a
qualified name exactly). One JSON object on stdout.
`crates/blue-lang-cli/tests/ast_resolved.rs` pins the exact output and fails
if a field here is undocumented. A migration is proven on it: a program whose
`flat` and `ns` trees are equal means the same thing under either rule.

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `namespace` | the entry file's bidama (from the Bluefile beside it), or `null` for the root namespace |
| `flat` | the entry file's top-level forms, resolved under the flat rule: each definition renamed to its runtime key (`retsu/first`; `%root/f` for a script) and each reference to what the rule binds it to (a builtin stays bare) |
| `ns` | the same forms under per-bidama namespaces |
| `references` | every non-local reference in the entry file |
| `imports` | the entry file's `use` declarations: the location fields, `package`, and `names` (the list, empty for a whole-package `use`) |
| `first_line` | the first line of the entry file's first top-level form, or `null` |
| `definitions` | the entry file's top-level definitions: the location fields and `name` |
| `builtins` | every name the interpreter binds, sorted |
| `reserved` | the reserved words, which no definition can be named |

Each entry of `references` carries the location fields of `blue check` and:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `top_level` | the index of the top-level form it is in |
| `written` | the symbol as the tree has it: `first`, or `retsu/first` for `retsu::first` |
| `opaque` | inside a macro call's arguments |
| `flat`, `ns` | what each rule binds it to |
| `locals` | the locals in scope where it is written, innermost first |
| `position` | `call` (the head of a call), `value` (anywhere else in code), `place` (the name `set!` rebinds) or `syntax` (a macro head, a template symbol) |
| `argc` | for a `call`, how many arguments it passes; `null` otherwise |
| `nullary` | what `ns` binds it to takes exactly zero parameters: a bare `value` reference is CALLED, and a `call` with `argc` 0 is B0023 |

This list is how a definition's callers are found: bare calls have no
parentheses, so searching the text for `name(` misses every one.

A binding (`flat`, `ns`) has:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `def` (a program definition), `builtin`, `local`, `ambiguous` (two imports list it) or `unbound` |
| `namespace` | the defining bidama for a `def`; `null` otherwise, and for the root namespace |
| `name` | the definition's or builtin's name |
| `key` | the symbol the resolved tree writes, or `null` when it keeps the written one |

## `blue query`

`blue query QUERY [PATH…]` lists every definition under the paths (files, or
directories of `.b` files; `.` when none) that satisfies a query: one line per
hit, `file:line:col: definition`, then what the pattern bound, then the chain
through which the definition reaches each capability a `reaches` clause names.
The engine answers it (`blue_lang_mondou::Engine::query`), each file loaded as
`blue check FILE` and the language server load it, so an editor or agent door
gets the same hits. A file whose imports do not load has no
resolved tree; it is named on stderr and the exit is 1.

A query is tatara-lisp data. Several clauses are their conjunction:

| clause | holds for a definition when |
|---|---|
| `(match PATTERN)` | a form of its resolved tree matches `PATTERN`; each matching form is a hit, with what the pattern bound |
| `(reaches CAP)` | it names a primitive of host capability `CAP` (`process`, `filesystem`, `environment`, `clock`, `network`; `host` for any), directly or through the definitions it references |
| `(annotated)`, `(unannotated)` | it is, or is not, a typed definition |
| `(calls NAME)` | a reference in it resolves to `NAME`: `retsu/first` or `retsu::first` for a bidama's definition, `%root/f` for a script's own, `first` for the builtin |
| `(package NAME)` | it is defined in bidama `NAME` |
| `(longer-than N)` | its tree has more than `N` forms |
| `(kind K)` | it is a `function`, `macro` or `value` |
| `(and C …)`, `(or C …)`, `(not C)` | the connectives |

A pattern is tatara's `match` pattern, compiled by tatara's own matcher. A
quasipattern reads as the code it matches: `` `(retsu/first ,xs) `` is a call
to retsu's `first` with one argument, bound to `xs`; outside an unquote a
symbol matches itself, `,_` matches anything, a final `,@rest` matches the
remaining elements, and `,(? string? s)` runs a predicate (under a pure frame
and a step budget; a predicate naming a host primitive or `eval` is refused).
Patterns see the resolved tree, the `ns` tree of `blue ast --resolved --json`:
every reference is written as what it resolved to, so a call written `first`
after `use("retsu", [:first])` and one written `retsu::first` are both
`retsu/first`, and a local named `first` is neither. A function definition's
own `(name params…)` is not a call and is not searched.

`--json` prints one object per hit per line:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `file`, `line`, `column` | where the matching form starts, or the definition when no pattern placed the hit |
| `definition` | the definition's name as written |
| `key` | its runtime key: `retsu/first`, `%root/f` |
| `kind` | `function`, `macro` or `value` |
| `bindings` | each name the pattern bound, and its value as tatara-lisp text |
| `reach` | each host capability the definition reaches, and one chain to it: the definitions it goes through, then the primitive |

A Bluefile names a query with `query(name, text)`, and `blue query NAME` runs
it from the project's directory or below:

```text
query("host_unannotated", "(reaches host) (unannotated)")
```

Over blue's own standard bidamas (2026-10-28, 255 files):

```text
$ blue query '(reaches filesystem)' bidamas
bidamas/isshou/anaritikusu/anaritikusu.b:2131:1: write_history  filesystem via write_file
bidamas/isshou/anaritikusu/anaritikusu.b:2488:1: example_append  filesystem via nisshi/el_append -> nisshi/write -> append_file
…
146 hit(s) in 255 file(s)

$ blue query '(match `(retsu/first ,xs))' bidamas/zumen
bidamas/koubou/zumen/zumen.b:147:14: layer_names  xs = l
1 hit(s) in 1 file(s)
```

`(annotated)` over the same corpus finds nothing: no bidama definition is
typed yet.

---

Source: `docs/GLOSSARY.md`

# Glossary: blue's terms and the concepts they name

blue names many of its parts in Japanese or in its own words. This page maps
each name to the standard concept you already know. Each table row gives the
concept in bold, one sentence on what blue does, and the page that owns the
term. A name from Japanese carries its kanji and its literal gloss. A row
marked **design** describes something that is not built.

Every entry is read from the code and the docs on 2026-10-30. When an entry
and its owning page disagree, the owning page is right: fix this page.

## The language and its files

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| blue | **A general-purpose, gradually typed language.** Its surface reads like Ruby and Elixir, it parses to a tatara-lisp tree, and a Rust runtime runs that tree. [introduction.md](docs/introduction.md) |
| `.b` | **The source-file extension.** Every blue program, script and bidama file ends in `.b`. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| `blue-lang-*` | **The crate prefix.** blue's Rust crates carry it because the bare name `blue` is taken on crates.io. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| tatara-lisp | **The intermediate representation, an s-expression tree.** The parser lowers every blue program to a tatara-lisp tree, and the `tatara-lisp-eval` crate evaluates it. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
| the pipeline (parse → check → erase → run) | **The compiler driver's fixed phase order.** `blue_lang_runtime::pipeline` owns the order, because erase before check and run before check both turn the checker off without an error. [pipeline.rs](crates/blue-lang-runtime/src/pipeline.rs) |
| parse | **Lexing and parsing to an AST.** `blue-lang-syntax` lexes the surface and lowers it to a spanned tatara-lisp tree. [blue-lang-syntax](crates/blue-lang-syntax/Cargo.toml) |
| check | **Static analysis: name resolution, lints and type checks in one stage.** The check stage runs every `RULES` row on every door, so an error-severity rule stops a program before it runs. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| erase | **Type erasure.** The erase stage deletes each annotation after the check stage reads it, so an annotated and an unannotated definition run as the same tree. [erase.rs](crates/blue-lang-runtime/src/erase.rs) |
| run | **Evaluation by a tree-walking interpreter.** `tatara-lisp-eval` walks the erased tree; a bytecode VM exists, but `blue run` does not use it. [COMPILE-TIME.md](docs/COMPILE-TIME.md) |
| lowering | **Desugaring.** A shorthand is defined by the longer form it rewrites to: `x++` lowers to `x += 1`, which lowers to `x = x + 1`. [CANONICAL-FORMS.md](docs/CANONICAL-FORMS.md) |
| door | **A front end, or an entry point into the compiler.** A door is one way into the pipeline: `blue run`, `blue test`, `blue check`, the language server or a bidama build. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| script | **A single-file program.** A `.b` file that opens with `#!/usr/bin/env blue` runs with every standard bidama and no Bluefile. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| project | **A package root with a manifest.** `blue new NAME` writes a Bluefile, its lock, a stub `flake.nix`, a bidama and a `main.b`. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| `def main()` | **The program entry point.** `blue run` calls `main` after the top level; `blue test`, `blue check` and `use` never call it. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| session (`eval`, `repl`, `serve`) | **A sandboxed REPL.** A session refuses code that reaches the host unless it starts with `--allow`, and `--budget STEPS` bounds each evaluation. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| distribution | **The standard library that ships inside the binary.** The distribution is the set of bidamas compiled into `blue`, so a script can `use` them with no install. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| `BLUE_PATH`, `BLUE_DIST` | **The module search path.** `use` looks in the project's `packages` roots, then `BLUE_PATH`, then `BLUE_DIST`, then the compiled-in distribution. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| zenbu (全部, *all of it*) | **A facade, or meta-package.** zenbu depends on every bidama in the distribution, as one dependency. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| macro (`defmacro`) | **A non-hygienic Lisp macro.** A program's own macro expands while the program runs, after the check stage; hygiene by construction is **design**. [COMPILE-TIME.md](docs/COMPILE-TIME.md) |

## Packages, manifests and builds

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| bidama (ビー玉, *glass marble*) | **A package.** A bidama is a directory of `.b` files with a Bluefile, a version and its own namespace; the word replaces "package" in blue's surface and tools. [blue-lang-bidama](crates/blue-lang-bidama/src/lib.rs) |
| Bluefile | **A package manifest that is also a build file (`Cargo.toml` and `build.rs` in one).** A Bluefile is a blue program; its words record facts, and it runs in a frame that binds only those words. [bluefile.rs](crates/blue-lang-pkg/src/bluefile.rs) |
| Bluefile word | **A manifest key.** Each word (`package`, `needs`, `generate`, `service`, `allow`, …) is one row of `WORDS` in `blue-lang-pkg`, with its signature and what it records. [REFERENCE.md](docs/REFERENCE.md) |
| Bluefile.lock | **A lockfile that holds the evaluated manifest.** It is blue's evaluation of the Bluefile as JSON, so nix reads it and never runs blue. [lock.rs](crates/blue-lang-pkg/src/lock.rs) |
| `blue lock` | **Lockfile generation plus a permission check.** It evaluates the Bluefile, derives `needs` from the `use` forms, pins each `source` with `nix flake prefetch`, checks the capability lattice, and writes no lock when the check fails. [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| `needs` | **A dependency with a version range.** `blue lock` derives a bidama's needs from its `use` forms; a Bluefile `needs` row only narrows a range (B0019). [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| version solver | **A dependency resolver.** `blue-lang-pkg` searches by backtracking with conflict attribution, not PubGrub, and stops at a step bound. [solve.rs](crates/blue-lang-pkg/src/solve.rs) |
| `use("pkg")` | **An import.** `use("retsu")` makes `retsu::name` reachable; `use("retsu", [:first])` also binds `first` bare in this file. [NAMESPACES.md](docs/NAMESPACES.md) |
| namespace | **A module namespace.** Each bidama is a namespace: a file reaches another bidama's definition qualified or listed in `use`, never bare (B0012). [NAMESPACES.md](docs/NAMESPACES.md) |
| `pkg::name`, `a::b::c`, `blue::name` | **A qualified name, as deep as the levels of a bidama go.** A qualified name skips the resolution tiers; `blue::first` names the builtin even past a definition of the same name. [NAMESPACES.md](docs/NAMESPACES.md) |
| resolution tiers | **Scope-resolution order.** A bare name is a local, else the file's own bidama's definition, else a listed name, else a builtin or master verb; `blue explain-name` shows each tier. [NAMESPACES.md](docs/NAMESPACES.md) |
| `legacy_names` | **A deprecated alias with a sunset.** A renamed definition keeps its old name as a bridge until the next minor version, and `blue migrate` rewrites the callers. [NAMESPACES.md](docs/NAMESPACES.md) |
| `generate` and `nix run .#regen` | **A code-generation target with a freshness check.** `generate(name, output, program)` names a committed file that a blue program writes; `checks.generated-<name>-fresh` fails on a stale copy, and `nix run .#regen` rewrites it. [Bluefile](Bluefile) |
| `checks.<name>` | **A CI test target.** A Bluefile `check(name, file)` becomes a nix flake check that runs `blue test` on the file. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| registry (sui, FlakeHub) | **A package registry.** A Bluefile `registry` entry renders the publish workflow for sui (first) or FlakeHub (optional); the lock stays the source of truth. [REGISTRY.md](docs/REGISTRY.md) |
| `Cargo.gen.lock` | **A committed Nix build spec for Cargo, in the crate2nix family.** It is a delta of `Cargo.lock` that lets substrate build with no import-from-derivation; `gen build .` regenerates it. [CARGO-GEN-LOCK.md](docs/CARGO-GEN-LOCK.md) |
| consumer | **A downstream dependent.** A consumer is a pleme-io repository with `.b` files; `blue gen/consumers.b sweep` runs this blue's `fmt --check` and `check` over each one. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
| `git land` | **A merge queue.** `git land` pushes HEAD to `land/<slug>`; CI runs on that commit, and a green run fast-forwards `main`. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
| pre-push gate | **A pre-push hook.** `gen/prepush.b` runs the fast gates that the changed paths select; `BLUE_PREPUSH_OFF=1` turns it off. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |

## Rigor: the blueshift and the typing ladder

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| blueshift | **Gradual typing as a continuum.** The blueshift is a program's position between loose (the tatara-lisp end) and locked (the Rust end); each declaration moves it toward Rust, and `blue shift` reports it. [climb-the-blueshift.md](docs/howto/climb-the-blueshift.md) |
| rung | **A strictness level.** A rung is a named position on the blueshift: dynamic (0), annotated (1), checked (2) or restricted (3); a file stands on the lowest rung its declarations justify. [shift.rs](crates/blue-lang-lsp/src/shift.rs) |
| restricted (rung 3) | **Hermetic build-time evaluation.** A restricted file is checked, and its macro phase reads only declared, content-addressed build inputs. [shift.rs](crates/blue-lang-lsp/src/shift.rs) |
| typing ladder | **Pay-as-you-go type checking.** The checker visits no node of an unannotated program and checks only the structure that is declared. [blue-lang-check](crates/blue-lang-check/src/lib.rs) |
| `Dyn` | **The dynamic type (`any`).** `Dyn` is the top type and the default, so unannotated code is less analysed, never less correct. [blue-lang-check](crates/blue-lang-check/src/lib.rs) |
| seam | **A runtime cast at a typed/untyped boundary, as gradual typing inserts.** When typed code receives an argument of unknown type, the checker records a seam (a runtime check at that call), and `blue check` lists it. [blue-lang-check](crates/blue-lang-check/src/lib.rs) |
| unsafe seam | **An FFI boundary that holds Rust `unsafe`.** blue allows `unsafe` only at one audited seam per foreign ABI; `blue-lang-kiwari` enforces this today, and a workspace-wide deny is **design**. [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| FORM axis | **One canonical syntax, as gofmt gives, extended to spelling.** Each thing has one spelling, the shortest that stays distinct, and every tool writes it. [CANONICAL-FORMS.md](docs/CANONICAL-FORMS.md) |
| RIGOR axis | **Opt-in static analysis.** Types, memory and capability limits slide per declaration: declare nothing and get no analysis. [theory/BLUE.md](https://github.com/pleme-io/theory/blob/main/BLUE.md) |
| canonical spelling | **The formatter's one chosen syntax.** blue reads older or borrowed spellings (`&&`, `unless`, `x.f(y)`) and writes one; `blue fmt --write` and `blue check --fix` rewrite a file to it. [CANONICAL-FORMS.md](docs/CANONICAL-FORMS.md) |
| the mark (blueshift ramp) | **The logo.** The mark is four solid cells across Nord's Frost band, `nord7` to `nord10`: a shift in colour, not in density. [blue-lang-art](crates/blue-lang-art/src/lib.rs) |
| irodori | **The fleet's colour-palette library (Nord).** `blue-lang-art` reads every colour from the `irodori` crate, and blue carries no hex of its own. [blue-lang-art](crates/blue-lang-art/src/lib.rs) |

## Frames, capabilities and postures

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| waku (枠, *frame*) | **An execution context that holds a capability set.** A waku says what a computation may depend on, in three parts (REACH, WHEN, WHERE); its only operation is `narrow`, and narrow cannot widen. [blue-lang-waku](crates/blue-lang-waku/src/lib.rs) |
| REACH | **The set of bound capabilities.** REACH is what a computation may name; a name outside it is an absent binding, not a call-time check. [blue-lang-waku](crates/blue-lang-waku/src/lib.rs) |
| WHEN | **The evaluation phase (staging).** WHEN says what has already run: `sealed` (nothing; no resident evaluator), `preceding` (earlier forms only, the macro phase) or `anytime` (`eval` allowed). [blue-lang-waku](crates/blue-lang-waku/src/lib.rs) |
| WHERE | **The memory region.** WHERE is the heap a computation uses: an arena freed at scope exit, its process's own heap, or shared frozen data. [blue-lang-waku](crates/blue-lang-waku/src/lib.rs) |
| `narrow` | **A monotonic privilege drop (a lattice meet).** `narrow` returns the meet of a frame and a bound, and no method returns a frame above its receiver. [blue-lang-waku](crates/blue-lang-waku/src/lib.rs) |
| capability | **An object capability, kept as a closed enum.** A capability is a named bundle of identifiers that a frame may grant; the six host capabilities are `process`, `filesystem`, `environment`, `clock`, `network` and `entropy`. [capability.rs](crates/blue-lang-waku/src/capability.rs) |
| floor (`reach`) | **The permissions a dependency requires.** A bidama's floor is the set of host capabilities its code names, or its declared `reach(%i[…])`, which must cover them. [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| ceiling (`allow`) | **The permissions an application grants.** Only the root declares a ceiling, with `allow(%i[…])`; a bidama never declares one. [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| the lattice check | **Permission resolution over the dependency closure.** `blue lock` joins every floor in the closure, checks `⋁ floors ⊑ allow ∨ provided`, and names the path to each package that breaks it. [capabilities.rs](crates/blue-lang-pkg/src/capabilities.rs) |
| `--allow CAP` | **A sandbox flag, like Deno's `--allow-*`.** `blue run --allow` or a shebang `--allow` holds a run to `none`, `host` or the named capabilities, and it only narrows a project's `allow`. [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| ambient | **Ambient authority.** A run with no `--allow`, outside a project that declares `allow` or `virtualize`, reaches every host capability; this is still the default of `blue run`. [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| hold | **A runtime permission policy.** The hold binds each withheld host name to a breach and each virtualized name to its provider, for the run and every process it spawns. [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| breach | **A fatal permission violation.** A breach raises an error that no `rescue` or `ensure` sees, and `blue run` exits 77 (`EX_NOPERM`). [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| `virtualize` | **A test double for a system resource, injected by the manifest.** `virtualize(cap, {using: …})` binds a host capability to a pure provider, for the whole program or `for:` the named packages. [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| provider | **A deterministic stand-in implementation.** The providers are `deterministic_stepped` (clock), `seeded_prng` (entropy), and `in_memory_overlay` or `null_sink` (filesystem); process, network and environment have none. [provision.rs](crates/blue-lang-waku/src/provision.rs) |
| posture (frame) | **A point in the permission and staging lattice.** A posture is a waku position; the Bluefile word `posture(when)` declares a package's WHEN floor, `"sealed"`, `"preceding"` or `"anytime"`. [bluefile.rs](crates/blue-lang-pkg/src/bluefile.rs) |
| engine posture | **The permission set of an embedded interpreter.** `Load::posture(allowed)` in `blue-lang-host` binds every host effect it does not allow as a refusal. [SERVICE-ACCESS.md](docs/SERVICE-ACCESS.md) |
| morphology (`blue morph`) | **A feature matrix of language modes.** It maps each posture to the qualities it grants and forfeits, and lists the pairs that truly exclude each other. [theory/BLUE.md](https://github.com/pleme-io/theory/blob/main/BLUE.md) |
| appliance (`blue bundle`) | **A sealed single-file executable.** `blue bundle FILE --runner blue-appliance` seals the compiled program and its lock's capability record onto a runner, which checks the BLAKE3 digest and runs held to that record. [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md) |
| pure, volatile | **Purity (effect) analysis.** mondou marks a definition pure only when its answer depends on its arguments alone; a host call, another effect, nondeterminism or an outer mutation makes it volatile. [reach.rs](crates/blue-lang-mondou/src/reach.rs) |

## Diagnostics, rules and ratchets

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| B-code (`B0001` …) | **A compiler error code, like rustc's `E0382`.** Each B-code is a `RULES` row with a slug, a severity, a law, a witness and a fix kind; `blue explain CODE` prints it. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| `RULES` | **The lint registry.** Every rule blue enforces is a row in one table in `blue-lang-check`, and the check stage runs it, so no door skips it. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| witness | **A failing fixture.** A rule's witness is a short program that breaks the rule, and the rule must flag it. [rules.rs](crates/blue-lang-check/src/rules.rs) |
| waiver (`# waive CODE: reason`) | **A lint suppression with a required reason, like `#[allow]`.** A waiver above a definition silences one code; a waiver with no reason (B0007) or one that silences nothing (B0008) is an error. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| project rule (`R0001` …) | **A custom lint, written in the project's own language.** `rule(code, file, def)` names a blue definition that gets each top-level form as data and returns findings; `blue check` runs it in a pure frame under a step budget. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| okite (掟, *the rules one lives by*) | **Architecture decision records with executable properties.** okite keeps each decision as a record (id, date, rule, why) with the laws that enforce it; the build fails when a decision has no law or a law fails. [RULES.md](bidamas/okite/RULES.md) |
| D-code (`D0004` …) | **A decision ID.** A D-code names one okite decision; D0004 says that `nil` and `[]` are different values. [RULES.md](bidamas/okite/RULES.md) |
| law | **A property-based test.** A law is a blue function that returns true when a rule holds; the generative laws run over hundreds of seeded values. [okite.b](bidamas/okite/okite.b) |
| ratchet | **A baseline that may only shrink (a "no new violations" gate).** A rule with `ratchet: Some(n)` counts its findings without failing; the commit that reaches zero makes it an error on every door. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| census (`blue census`) | **A violation counter for a staged lint rollout.** `blue census ROOT` counts each finding of every rule still ratcheting in, and `checks.namespace-census` fails unless each count equals its row's ratchet exactly. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| hadome (歯止め, *ratchet pawl*) | **A baseline file with a ratchet judge.** hadome reads a `<kind>: <key> <size>` baseline and judges each measurement unrecorded, held or grew, so recorded debt shrinks or holds and never grows. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| `blue check --fix` | **An autofix, like `cargo fix` or `eslint --fix`.** It applies every machine-applicable fix the rules carry. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| `blue migrate` | **A codemod.** It makes each implicit reference to another bidama explicit, and it keeps a file only when its resolved tree is unchanged. [NAMESPACES.md](docs/NAMESPACES.md) |
| form is the producer's | **Per-package editions, as Rust judges each crate by its own edition.** A dependency compiles as written and is judged on meaning only, so a consumer never fails because a dependency is written for another blue. [COMPOUNDING.md](docs/COMPOUNDING.md) |
| seal tier | **The strength of a guarantee.** blue grades each prevented bad state, from truly unrepresentable through parse-time-rejected and CI-caught to only mitigated, and names the ceiling of each weak grade. [VOCABULARIFY-SURFACE.md](docs/VOCABULARIFY-SURFACE.md) |
| DESIGN tier | **A "proposed" status.** A DESIGN row is stated and not built; work that builds against one says so. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| blind | **An inconclusive result.** A probe that cannot observe reports blind, which counts apart and never as a pass. [spec/README.md](spec/README.md) |

## Tools and the engine

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| mondou (問答, *question and answer*) | **A memoized query engine on the salsa and rust-analyzer model.** Every tool asks mondou the same queries, and it computes each answer once: a parse per text, an analysis per document revision, a bidama per session; it is hand-written (no salsa crate), and salsa-style early cutoff is **design**. [blue-lang-mondou](crates/blue-lang-mondou/src/lib.rs) |
| language server (`blue lsp`) | **An LSP server.** `blue-lang-lsp` is a transport-free analysis core over mondou plus a JSON-RPC stdio shim; it adds a `blue/shift` request for the blueshift. [blue-lang-lsp](crates/blue-lang-lsp/src/lib.rs) |
| `blue serve` | **An editor protocol for live evaluation, like nREPL.** It serves one evaluation session as JSON lines on stdin and stdout. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| `blue query` | **A code query language, like CodeQL or Semgrep.** It lists every definition a query matches over the resolved tree, with forms such as `(match PATTERN)` and `(reaches CAP)`. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| `def_hash` | **A content hash of a resolved definition, as Unison uses.** mondou hashes each definition's resolved tree, and the call memo keys pure calls by it. [blue-lang-mondou](crates/blue-lang-mondou/src/lib.rs) |
| recall | **Automatic memoization of pure functions.** mondou answers a call it proves pure from the `def_hash` and the arguments; it is off unless a door turns it on. [recall.rs](crates/blue-lang-mondou/src/recall.rs) |
| `blue fmt` | **A formatter with no options, like gofmt.** `blue-lang-fmt` gives one output per program, and no configuration surface exists. [CANONICAL-FORMS.md](docs/CANONICAL-FORMS.md) |
| kiwari (木割, *the carpenter's proportioning rule-book*) | **A single-source grammar specification.** kiwari holds blue's one grammar as data and renders tree-sitter's `grammar.js` and queries from it; `blue-lang-kiwari` holds that grammar equal to blue's own parser. [NATURALIZE-TREESITTER.md](docs/NATURALIZE-TREESITTER.md) |
| kigou (記号, *symbol*) | **A Unicode character-class and operator-alias table.** kigou decides what each non-ASCII character means: an alias of an operator blue has (`≠` is `!=`), part of a name (`λ`), or a lex error. [VOCABULARIFY-SURFACE.md](docs/VOCABULARIFY-SURFACE.md) |
| yakugo (訳語, *equivalent term*) | **Localized keywords, a non-English surface syntax.** A yakugo pack rewrites identifier tokens before the parser, so `définir … fin` gives the same tree as `def … end`. [VOCABULARIFY-SURFACE.md](docs/VOCABULARIFY-SURFACE.md) |
| surface | **A concrete-syntax skin over one AST.** A surface is the human language a program is written in, and kigou and yakugo are its vocabulary; `BLUE_LANG` selects it, and an unknown tag is an error. [VOCABULARIFY-SURFACE.md](docs/VOCABULARIFY-SURFACE.md) |
| sabi (錆, *rust*) | **A Rust code generator.** sabi renders Rust source from blue data; it writes kigou's tables into `blue-lang-syntax`. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| `blue-lang-host` | **An embedding API, like the Lua C API or mlua.** A Rust program adds one dependency and a `#[host]` impl block, and calls blue definitions with typed values. [blue-lang-host](crates/blue-lang-host/Cargo.toml) |
| `blue-lang-wasm` | **A WebAssembly target with no imports.** It compiles blue to a module with no host imports and no WASI. [blue-lang-wasm](crates/blue-lang-wasm/Cargo.toml) |
| `blue-lang-component` | **A WASI preview 2 component.** It is the blue engine as one WASI command component that runs one blue service program. [BUILD-STACK.md](docs/BUILD-STACK.md) |

## Testing

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| `test` block | **An inline unit test, like Rust's `#[test]` in the same file.** A `test "name" … end` block sits beside its code; `blue run` drops it, and `blue test` runs each block in its own forked interpreter. [test-and-doctest.md](docs/howto/test-and-doctest.md) |
| doctest | **An executable doc example, as in Rust and Elixir.** An indented `expr #=> value` line in a `@doc` is a test, and `blue test` runs it beside the `test` blocks. [test-and-doctest.md](docs/howto/test-and-doctest.md) |
| `@doc`, `@moduledoc` | **Doc comments as typed values, as in Elixir.** `@moduledoc` opens a bidama with its purpose and an example, and `@doc` documents one definition; B0056–B0060 refuse a missing, empty or restated one. [DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| hermetic `blue test` | **Test isolation from the host.** `blue test` drops the inherited `GIT_DIR` family, refuses a write outside `TMPDIR`, and gives a Bluefile check only its declared inputs under `GEN_ROOT`, as the nix sandbox does; `BLUE_TEST_ENV=inherit`, `BLUE_TEST_WRITES=anywhere` and `BLUE_INPUTS=checkout` turn each off. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| tesuto (テスト, *test*) | **Assertion helpers and snapshot tests.** tesuto checks that a function raises a given error kind, and compares a value with its stored snapshot. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| test-beside | **A coverage gate per definition.** `checks.test-beside` fails when a package has more definitions that no test reaches than its recorded hadome debt; `waive(name, why, until)` excuses one. [TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md) |
| heni (変異, *mutation*) | **Mutation testing, like cargo-mutants.** heni changes one literal in a fresh copy of a package and runs its tests, which must fail; each mutation ends caught, survived, refused or blind. [TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md) |
| conformance row | **A conformance test, like test262.** A row in `spec/rows/` states one observable behaviour, and every evaluator must agree with stage 0 on it. [spec/README.md](spec/README.md) |
| evaluator column | **Differential testing across implementations.** The suite runs each row on `walker`, `vm`, `wasm`, `cli`, `static`, `memo` and `component`, and a column that disagrees with its reference fails; `component` is judged against `cli`, so one program run in two placements must give the same output and failure. [spec/README.md](spec/README.md) |
| `pending("<gap>")` | **A strict expected failure (strict xfail).** A pending row names its gap and fails the run when the gap closes, until the mark is removed. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| second implementation (`*-diff` crates) | **An oracle for differential testing.** `blue-lang-yaml-diff` and `blue-lang-danpen-diff` run yaml-rust2 and apollo-compiler on the same corpus and compare the results with blue's. [blue-lang-yaml-diff](crates/blue-lang-yaml-diff/Cargo.toml) |

## Batteries and the verb graph

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| battery (lateral) | **A batteries-included module for one cross-cutting concern.** Each concern that every program carries (errors, retries, configuration, logs) is one bidama or primitive with one verb set; the full lateral map is **design**. [theory/BLUE.md](https://github.com/pleme-io/theory/blob/main/BLUE.md) |
| kyohi (拒否, *refusal*) | **Errors as values: a list of validation results.** A refusal is `[kind, why]`; `check` returns every refusal a subject has, and `enforce` raises them as one error. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| kousei (構成, *composition*) | **Declarative configuration with per-entry validation.** A declaration is a list of entries, each checked, configured `off`, tuned or refused alone; `judge` sorts them into accepted, off and refused, so one bad entry never fails its siblings. [kousei.b](bidamas/kousei/kousei.b) |
| settei (設定, *settings*) | **Layered configuration, twelve-factor style.** `settei::read(app, defaults)` resolves the defaults, then `~/.config/<app>/<app>.yaml`, then `<APP>_<GROUP>__<KEY>` variables, each typed by its default. [settei.b](bidamas/settei/settei.b) |
| shisei (姿勢, *posture*) | **A middleware stack with secure defaults.** A service posture is a kousei entry whose layer wraps a handler; each one runs by default, and one that can refuse a request has an audit-or-enforce mode. [shisei.b](bidamas/eigyou/shisei/shisei.b) |
| bougyo (防御, *defence*) | **Request-defence middleware, like Helmet plus request limits.** bougyo adds security headers and a request id and limits method, path, headers and body; `limits` defaults to `audit`. [bougyo.b](bidamas/eigyou/bougyo/bougyo.b) |
| saishikou (再試行, *retrying*) | **Retry with exponential backoff.** `saishikou::retrying(policy, step)` calls `step` again after a doubling pause, up to `times` calls, for the error kinds in `on`; it holds no supervisor restart policy. [saishikou.b](bidamas/saishikou/saishikou.b) |
| mokuroku (目録, *catalogue*) | **A package index with API docs.** mokuroku reads every bidama on a `BLUE_PATH` (manifest, gloss, tests, each `def` with its `@doc`), and it holds the verb-graph rows. [mokuroku.b](bidamas/mokuroku/mokuroku.b) |
| hon (本, *book*) | **A documentation generator, rustdoc and mdBook in one.** hon reads the Diátaxis pages, the `@doc` attributes and the Bluefile, and renders the reference, the book, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the llms files; the static site is **design**. [DOCUMENTATION.md](docs/DOCUMENTATION.md) |
| Diátaxis kind | **The document type.** Each page under `docs/` declares `kind: tutorial`, `howto`, `reference` or `explanation`, and `checks.docs` refuses a page with none. [DOCUMENTATION.md](docs/DOCUMENTATION.md) |
| verb graph | **A registry of the library's operations, a typed API vocabulary.** Each verb is a row in `bidamas/mokuroku/graph/`, one file per space, and `blue verbs check` gates the graph against a recorded baseline; the roadmap that fills it is **design**. [DESIGN.md](docs/verbs/H/DESIGN.md) |
| space | **A module, or protocol namespace, for verbs.** A space groups the verbs of one subject, called as `space::verb`; a provisional space ends in `?`. [VERB-ROADMAP.md](docs/VERB-ROADMAP.md) |
| verb contract | **An interface signature shared by every module that has the verb.** `contracts.tsv` gives each verb one argument shape, one return shape and one error behaviour across spaces. [contracts.tsv](docs/verbs/contracts.tsv) |
| `need`, `get` | **The raising and the nil-returning accessor.** `need` raises when the value is absent and `get` returns `nil`; blue never names a `_or` variant. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| master verb | **A generic function with dynamic dispatch, like a protocol.** A master verb such as `has?`, `delete` or `diff` dispatches on its subject's space, and `verb_for` registers a space's handler. [REFERENCE.md](docs/REFERENCE.md) |
| retsu (列, *row*) | **List utilities made total.** `size`, `first`, `rest` and `is_empty` accept `nil` and `[]` alike. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| deeta (データ, *data*) | **A JSON and YAML library.** deeta parses JSON and YAML 1.2, reads nested values safely and writes JSON or YAML. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| kueri (クエリ, *query*) | **A query builder that renders SQL.** kueri holds analysis as a query IR in blue and renders SQL for DuckDB. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| kazu, shuugou, kansuu, jisho | **Numbers, sets, function combinators and maps.** These are the small core bidamas the agent guide names in its traps (数, 集合, 関数, 辞書). [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| kirikae (切り替え, *switching over*) | **A NixOS switch planner.** kirikae decides whether a system switch must run, may be skipped or must wait, and it is settei's worked example. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |

## Services and deployment

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| `service(...)` | **A service declaration, like a Compose service.** One Bluefile word states the program, port, probes, config, access, runtime and bindings, and every deploy file is a rendering of it. [BUILD-STACK.md](docs/BUILD-STACK.md) |
| `access` | **A least-privilege manifest: a pod security context plus a NetworkPolicy.** `access` lists a service's effects, egress peers, read and write paths, listen ports and programs it runs; the engine posture is built, and most other renderings are **design**. [SERVICE-ACCESS.md](docs/SERVICE-ACCESS.md) |
| runtime rung (wasm, native) | **The deployment target.** A service runs as a WASI preview 2 component by default, and `runtime: :native, because: :<gap>` picks a native process for a named WASI gap (`process`, `host_program`, `device`). [BUILD-STACK.md](docs/BUILD-STACK.md) |
| haibi (配備, *deployment*) | **A Helm chart generator.** haibi renders a `service` into a chart with a closed, generated `values.schema.json`, its config defaults and, for a declared schema, the SQL migration. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| `blue workload render` | **Committed Kubernetes manifests for GitOps.** It renders a Bluefile `workload` into Kubernetes objects in committed, freshness-gated files. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| `blue image build` | **A container image build.** It builds a Bluefile `image` through nix and reports the tarball, its size and its layers. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| `blue diff --context` | **A read-only `kubectl diff`.** It compares the committed workload files with a cluster; no `blue apply` exists, because a GitOps reconciler applies the commit. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| placement | **A deployment-target binding, like a Kustomize overlay.** `placement(name, {node:})` or `{cluster:, namespace:}` says where a service runs, with per-place values; Flux objects per placement are **design**. [BUILD-STACK.md](docs/BUILD-STACK.md) |
| `blue-lang-proc` | **Erlang/OTP processes and supervisors.** Each process owns its VM and interpreter, a message is deep-copied, and a supervisor restarts children one-for-one, one-for-all, rest-for-one or simple-one-for-one; supervision as a service default is **design**. [blue-lang-proc](crates/blue-lang-proc/src/lib.rs) |
| kyuuji (給仕, *serving*) | **An HTTP/1.1 server loop.** kyuuji runs handlers as functions from a request to a response record, with a built-in health path, and answers a raise with 500. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| koutei (工程, *one production step*) | **A CI step toolkit, like `@actions/core`.** koutei reads `INPUT_*` inputs and writes outputs, step summaries and annotations; it is the `run.b` side of every blue action. [NAMES.md](bidamas/NAMES.md) |
| fueki (不易, *the unchanging*) | **Write once, deploy anywhere by placement.** An application is declared once, and each runtime (WASI, Nix, OCI, engenho, Helm) is a renderer that a placement datum selects. [theory/FUEKI.md](https://github.com/pleme-io/theory/blob/main/FUEKI.md) |

## Fleet terms the docs use

These are pleme-io names outside blue. blue's docs and agent guide use them.

| fleet term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| shikumi | **A typed configuration library.** It is the fleet's config library; `settei` is blue's form of it, and `BlueConfig` implements `shikumi::TieredConfig`. [agents.md](docs/agents.md) |
| substrate | **A Nix build-pattern library.** It builds blue's crates and holds the reusable `blue-project.yml` workflow. [BUILD-STACK.md](docs/BUILD-STACK.md) |
| sui | **A Nix build scheduler and binary cache.** It builds each change once on the build node, and every other machine substitutes. [BUILD-STACK.md](docs/BUILD-STACK.md) |
| engenho | **A Kubernetes runtime written in Rust.** It runs a service's chart on any node, and its wasm backend runs the component. [BUILD-STACK.md](docs/BUILD-STACK.md) |
| Flux | **A GitOps reconciler (FluxCD).** It applies the committed objects to a cluster. [BUILD-STACK.md](docs/BUILD-STACK.md) |
| Tela | **The fleet's frontend standard.** blue hosts a frontend framework that retargets Tela, and that framework is **design**. [theory/BLUE-FRONTEND.md](https://github.com/pleme-io/theory/blob/main/BLUE-FRONTEND.md) |

## Implementer terms

| blue term | standard concept |
|---|---|
| `INFIX` | **The operator-precedence table.** It is one table, and the parser and the formatter both read it, so a new operator is one new row. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
| lowered name: OWNED or DELEGATED | **A reserved internal name, or a runtime intrinsic.** An OWNED name (`blue-assert`) must not be bound by the runtime; a DELEGATED name (`hash-map`) must be. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
| the three arbiters | **Head resolution in a Lisp.** A special form, a macro or an environment binding can claim a name, and `Interpreter::resolve_head` says which one does. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
| `blue_lang_runtime::interpreter` | **The runtime initializer (the prelude).** It installs both runtime layers; a hand-rolled `Interpreter::new()` omits the Lisp standard library. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
| fork (`blue_lang_proc::forking`) | **A copy-on-write snapshot of an interpreter.** A fork shares the evaluated globals and isolates each child by its seal; a plain `Clone` is not a fork. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
| parking primitive | **A blocking call that suspends a process.** `receive` parks until a message is ready, and it must not take the message before it parks. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
| `format_source_lossless` | **A comment-preserving pretty-printer.** Every tool that shows a user their own file formats through it. [implementing.md](docs/implementing.md) |
